A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same VL-ICL Bench work. Their complete text, figures, tables, equations and appendices are readable, allowing retained, revised and added material to be matched.

before.justification: v1 reports original VLLM benchmark evaluations, image-generation results and analyses of shot scaling, prompting and instruction tuning in Section 4 and the appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds evaluations of further tasks and models, context extension and model-size scaling.

M1.justification: The work remains a benchmark using pretrained models and support/query prompting, without proposing a revised learning algorithm, architecture or objective. SelfExtend appears as an additional controlled evaluation of an existing technique.

E1.justification: The main suite expands from eight to ten tasks, adding Fast Counting and Fast Attribute Matching, which require generating images using newly learned count or attribute names. v2 also evaluates an artificial-label Fast Matching MiniImageNet variant; conventional Matching MiniImageNet results remain in Appendix Table 23.

E2.justification: v2 adds evaluated models including IDEFICS2, VILA, Mantis, Phi3-Vision, LongVA, LLaVA-OneVision and InternLM-XComposer2.5. Appendix Table 27 additionally evaluates Anole-7B on text-to-image MiniImageNet. LongVA and Mantis also join the retained many-shot comparisons in Tables 42–45.

E3.justification: v2 introduces peak accuracy, normalized ICL efficiency and average-rank summaries, plus controlled 4K-to-16K SelfExtend evaluations and LLaVA-OneVision comparisons at 0.5B, 7B and 72B parameters. The COCO judging protocol is inconsistently described: Section 2.2 now names GPT-3.5, while Table 12 retains v1's LLaVA-Next attribution, so an actual judge replacement is unresolved.

E4.justification: v2 adds context-extension and model-size studies, efficiency-versus-zero-shot analysis, and performance trends by model release date. It expands the existing 64-shot study to additional models. Earlier prompting, repetition and instruction-tuning analyses remain, while v1's aggregate per-shot accuracy-increment analysis is removed.

E5.justification: Both versions specify three random seeds and retain the same average and plus/minus reporting practices in detailed result tables. Additional rows extend these practices without introducing new uncertainty procedures, significance tests or an increased run count.

E6.justification: New tasks, models, metrics and controls add substantial results, and the expanded comparison identifies LLaVA-OneVision-72B instead of GPT4V as the overall image-to-text leader. LLaVA-Next-7B's 4-/5-shot Fast Open-Ended MiniImageNet entries change from 0.00/0.33 to 37.24/36.95 (v1 Table 12; v2 Table 16). However, v2 Table 54 retains the old values, preventing a clean performance-gain interpretation.

T1.justification: v2 defines ICL efficiency through normalized area above zero-shot performance and states the bound that zero-shot accuracy plus efficiency cannot exceed 100% (Section 4.1 and Appendix B.7). The original probabilistic ICL formulation remains unchanged; no substantial theorem or proof development is added.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and closing section retain the same central contributions: exposing limitations of VQA/captioning-based ICL evaluation, introducing a broad multimodal benchmark, and identifying VLLM strengths and weaknesses. The expanded experiments support this existing agenda.

C2.justification: v1 primarily attributes poor shot scaling to context and image-token limitations. v2 qualifies this explanation by arguing that context extension alone is insufficient, interprets model-size comparisons as evidence of an emergent ICL threshold, and discusses progress over release dates. Its Discussion also explicitly acknowledges limited text-to-image model coverage.

D1.justification: Appendix Table 6 expands configuration documentation with connection modules, image-token representations and context windows for newer models. Conversely, v2 removes v1's code/dataset access link and A100-80GB hardware disclosure. These are documentation changes; the PDFs do not establish that the resources became unavailable.

R1.justification: v2 adds recent model and SelfExtend references, cites additional multimodal ICL studies, and explicitly distinguishes its scope from Jiang et al. (2024b)'s recognition-focused many-shot evaluation. The existing related-work organization and principal novelty positioning remain intact.

P1.justification: v2 shortens the title and several task descriptions, folds Text Variation into a paragraph, renames Conclusion to Discussion, and relocates qualitative discussion to Appendix C. Most introductory prose, motivation and the main section sequence remain recognizable.

P2.justification: The main results presentation shifts to summary Tables 2–5 and selected curves. The updated radar plot moves earlier, while full benchmark curves and qualitative images move to the appendices. Figure 1 gains two task illustrations, and new model-size, efficiency, context-extension and temporal plots substantially expand the visual presentation.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially improves the benchmark's diagnostic value by experimentally probing context length and model size, addressing v1's largely conjectural explanation of shot-scaling failures. Added generation tasks and artificial-label matching broaden the learning abilities tested, while efficiency summaries distinguish adaptation from zero-shot competence. These gains outweigh the reduced reproducibility documentation and reporting inconsistencies, particularly conflicting LLaVA baseline entries and caption-judge attribution, which still require clarification.
